behavior: A migratory dabbling duck that forages in shallow water by surface-feeding, filtering mud, and tipping up. It flies rapidly and agilely, often gathering in flocks outside the breeding season.
field_marks: Very small, compact duck with a large head, short neck, and short tail
Adult male has a chestnut head with a broad iridescent-green patch behind the eye
Finely patterned gray body with a buff breast marked by dark spots
Short, narrow, dark bill and dark brown eye
Both sexes have a glossy green secondary-wing patch, often concealed when resting
Female is mottled brown and tan with a strong dark eyeline and grayish bill
habitat: Shallow freshwater and brackish wetlands, including marshes, wooded ponds, lakeshores, river margins, mudflats, estuaries, and flooded fields; nesting typically occurs in dense ground vegetation near water.
